about: What the Kotlin backend's `LuaScriptEngine` answers differently from
ECMA-262, case by case, against the shared table beside this file.
The engine is Lua with `EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` rewriting the
author's ECMAScript into Lua text. `EngineFactory` offers it beside
Rhino and QuickJS as an equal option, so a consumer may pick it; the
two others answer every case in the shared table.
This file is the Kotlin counterpart of `lua_engine_divergences.json`,
and it exists for the reason that one states: a count that lives in
prose is a count nobody re-answers. `EcmaScriptSemanticsTest` used to
assert only that the failure set was NOT EMPTY — satisfied by one
disagreement and by fifty — while `LuaScriptEngine`'s KDoc carried
"27 of its 58" under a sentence claiming that test held the number.
It held none, and the shared table had grown to 98 cases. Measured
with the list in place, the set is the 46 entries below.
Separate from the C++ list on purpose, and neither may be derived from
the other: this backend rewrites with its own transformer onto a
different Lua, so the sets are two measurements of two engines that
happen to share a strategy. They are not the same size — the C++
selection declares 23 — and the difference is itself a thing no prose
count could have shown.
An entry here that starts agreeing fails as loudly as a case that
starts disagreeing, so neither direction passes unnoticed.
`source` and `clause` together identify a case: the shared table asks
`a && b` under two clauses, and a list keyed on the expression alone
would let one declaration cover a divergence nobody looked at.
No `needs` field, unlike the C++ list. There it says what closing an
entry would take, and each value is an analysis of that rewriter.
Nobody has done that analysis for this one, and a guessed value would
be exactly the unmeasured claim this file was written to remove.
Adding it, entry by entry, is the next thing this list wants.
`diverges_on` says WHICH PATH into the engine an entry is about, the same
way `lua_engine_divergences.json` says it, and `paths` below is the set an
entry may name. Both are one value here, and that is a MEASUREMENT rather
than a formality: a backend reaches its Lua engine through the runtime
rewriter only while nothing lowers its expressions at build time, and this
backend's templates hand the engine the author's source at every site.
`ecma262_scoreboard_contract` derives the same answer from `sce-build`
(`Language::Kotlin.supports_script_engine_target`) and holds this key to
it, so the day the Kotlin templates cross the seam this file goes red
asking which path each of these 46 entries is still about — instead of
keeping 46 answers that quietly became ambiguous.
`build_time_frontend` says, for each entry, WHAT THE OTHER ROUTE ALREADY
ANSWERS. `diverges_on` names the path an entry is wrong on; this names
what the path it is not on would do with the same case, which is the
question a reader deciding whether to fund the seam actually has. The
block below declares its vocabulary and its tally, both re-derived by
`kotlin_lowering_dividend`.
What `sce-build`'s frontend already answers for each entry above,
measured on this backend's own Lua by `LoweredEcma262Test`.
The 46 entries are all one path — `runtime-rewriter` — because that
is the only route the generated Kotlin has. That says nothing about
how many of them the OTHER route would still get wrong, and the
difference is the whole case for moving translation to build time:
an entry the frontend already answers is one the seam retires, and
an entry the frontend also gets wrong is work the seam does not buy.
Until this field existed the two were indistinguishable in a list
whose only summary was its length.
Not derived from `diverges_on`, and it may not be. That key is about
the route an entry IS on; this one is a measurement of the route it
is NOT on, and no amount of reading the first answers the second —
the frontend's Lua had never been put to this backend's engine at
all until `LoweredEcma262Test` did it.
EVERY ENTRY CARRIES ONE. Unclassified is red rather than a default,
the same way `diverges_on` is: a missing value would silently mean
`unmeasured`, which is the one value that exempts an entry from the
measurement, and an exemption nothing has to justify is how a tally
stops being one.
THE TERMINAL STATE IS THAT THIS BLOCK IS GONE. It exists because
`build-time-lowering` is not yet a path this backend HAS, so the
answer cannot be written as a `diverges_on` entry. The day
`Language::Kotlin.supports_script_engine_target(Lua)` is true, that
key carries it and this one is redundant — so the lane named
below fails on exactly that day, naming the migration rather
than leaving a second vocabulary for the same fact.

values.answers: The frontend's Lua for this case runs on this backend's Lua engine and answers what ECMA-262 says. The seam retires this entry.
values.diverges: The frontend's Lua reaches the engine unchanged and the answer is still wrong. Declared in `kotlin_lowered_ecma262.json`'s `divergences`; the seam does not retire this entry, the frontend defect does.
values.unmeasured: The case cannot be put to the engine as the frontend wrote it — `EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` rewrites the frontend's own Lua on the way in, destructively. Declared in `kotlin_lowered_ecma262.json`'s `unreachable`; the answer is unknown until the lowered entry point exists.
